subject: Request: liability layering & pricing ask for pilot — need exec authorization
messages:
From: Evan Li <evan.li@nectarhealth.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nectarhealth.com>
Date: 2029-01-17T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: Liability layering and price adjustment for pilot

David —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement pushed back on two things before we can get to signatures for the 6-month pilot:

1) Liability cap — they want the vendor cap increased from your standard USD 1,000,000 to USD 3,000,000 for the pilot period.
2) Warranty & indemnity tweaks — legal is requesting the IP indemnity carve-out be expanded and a longer warranty window for performance defects (90 days -> 180 days).

Separately, procurement is asking if you can move on price: they expect a one-time pilot discount of 25% on the first 3 months to qualify this as a funded evaluation.

I've attached the latest SOW (NH-SOW-v3.pdf) with their redlines. Can you confirm whether these items require executive approval on your side and what the expected timeline is? We want to avoid last-minute delays — target signature by end of January.

Appreciate a quick read and next steps.

— Evan
Senior Procurement Manager
Nectar Health

Attachments: NH-SOW-v3.pdf

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Evan Li <evan.li@nectarhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-01-17T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Liability layering and price adjustment for pilot

Evan —

Thanks for the note and for sending the redlines. Quick status: we can discuss the pricing and a pilot concession, but the liability cap increase and the requested indemnity/warranty language are above the thresholds that require executive review here.

To help speed things along, please confirm:
- Is the requested USD 3,000,000 cap tied specifically to the pilot period only, or expected to carry into any paid renewal?
- The warranty extension to 180 days — is that for all SLA-covered items or only data-integrity/performance defects called out in the SOW?

I'll circulate the redlines to Deal Desk and Legal (copied), and draft a short decision memo. Marissa/Laura: legal flagged the IP/indemnity carve-outs as non-standard — need your guidance on whether we accept limited carve-outs or require exec sign-off for anything broader than IP-only indemnity. I'll attach a short summary for execs (redline_summary.xlsx).

Evan, I expect to come back with an internal recommendation by EOD tomorrow. If execs approve, we can proceed to DocuSign with the agreed SOW.

Best,
David Kim
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redline_summary.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-01-17T15:20:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: Liability layering and price adjustment for pilot — legal redlines need exec clearance

Forwarding Evan's thread with legal's quick read below. Key points from Legal:

- Liability cap increase to USD 3,000,000: material risk for larger deployments; acceptable for a short, capped pilot if timeboxed and tied to fees incurred during pilot. Legal recommends that any increase be approved by an Exec (CRO/CFO) and limited strictly to the pilot term.

- Indemnity: the request expands customer indemnity beyond IP and third-party claims to include broader product performance claims. Legal strongly recommends we limit indemnity to IP, data breaches caused by Redwood, and third-party claims — anything broader requires explicit exec sign-off.

- Warranty 180 days: Legal is unconvinced that a 180-day blanket warranty is appropriate for SaaS outputs; recommend compromise to 90 days for functional defects and a separate SLA for performance metrics.

I have annotated the SOW and attached the summary (redline_summary.xlsx) with recommended redline language. If Deal needs an executive decision memo, I can draft it — but will need a single proposed concession profile (liability cap amount for pilot + indemnity carveouts + discount threshold).

— Laura
Head of Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redline_summary.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-01-18T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Liability layering and price adjustment for pilot — legal redlines need exec clearance

Short answer: escalate.

Proposal for exec review (single ask):
- Liability cap: approve up to USD 3,000,000, strictly for the 6-month pilot and only to cover documented fees and direct damages.
- Indemnity: accept IP & data-breach indemnity; explicitly decline broader performance indemnity.
- Warranty: propose 90 days for defect remediation, with performance SLAs measured separately.
- Pricing: counter with 15% pilot concession (not 25%).

Priyom: please confirm the margin impact of a 15% concession on months 1–3 and whether finance will approve a one-time discount for this strategic reference customer. If finance signs off, I'll prepare a one-page memo for Marcus and the CFO to sign off.

Marissa
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Evan Li <evan.li@nectarhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-01-19T13:47:00-08:00
Subject: Decision and next steps: Nectar Health pilot — exec authorization outcome

Evan —

Update after internal review and a short exec review: thank you for your patience. Execs approved a narrowly scoped concession for the pilot with the following agreed terms:

1) Liability cap: REDWOOD will accept a pilot-specific cap of USD 3,000,000 limited to direct damages arising during the 6-month pilot term and capped to fees paid for the pilot period. This cap will not carry into any renewal or broader deployment unless separately agreed.

2) Indemnity: Redwood will accept an IP indemnity and indemnity for data breaches caused by Redwood. We will NOT accept broader performance indemnity (no indemnity for customer business loss from model outputs).

3) Warranty: 90-day warranty for remediation of functional defects; performance SLAs will be handled via the SOW milestones and a separate SLA appendix.

4) Pricing: approved one-time pilot concession of 15% for months 1–3 (counter to the 25% ask).

Next steps:
- Laura has prepared the redline language (attached in the internal summary).
- We'll update the SOW and route to DocuSign once you confirm the pilot-only nature of the cap and the 15% concession is acceptable.
- Please confirm whether Nectar wants the pilot pilot fees invoiced up-front or monthly; we can accommodate either, but the liability cap is scoped to fees actually paid.

Assignees: Marissa will finalize the decision memo; Priyom will confirm finance margin impact for the 15% concession in writing; Marcus Lin (cc'd) has reviewed and provided the final yes for this one-time exception.

If this is acceptable we will attach the agreed SOW and send a DocuSign package today.

Best regards,
David Kim
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments (internal): redline_summary.xlsx
